name: Source-Witness Criterion for Union-Closed Families
statement: For a nonempty union-closed family and fixed positive separator rows, witnesses at the sources of its directed one-inclusion graph extend continuously and rationally along every allowed one-element addition. Hence the row family is feasible exactly when witnesses exist at all graph sources. For well-graded families, the sources are precisely the inclusion-minimal members.
proof: Shrink all negative witness coordinates together, then turn the added coordinate positive with a finite-minimum choice. Union closure ensures only rows having that coordinate as their unique positive literal can oppose the change, and each such row already has a negative literal in the old concept.
